author: sjm41
body:
* **PTHR ID & PTN node:**
 PTN000746498 - ALCOHOL DEHYDROGENASE RELATED (PTHR11695)


* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
Dmel  Rtn4ip1 (FBgn0031500)
Human RTN4IP1 (Q8WWV3)

* **Type of Issue: Erroneous source or erroneous propagation, or other issue**
erroneous propagation

This node is annotated with 'alcohol dehydrogenase [NAD(P)+] activity' based on one annotation to YEAST\|SGD=S000004760\|UniProtKB=P28625).
That comes from PMID: 32967812, whose abstract includes:
Herein, we report that an uncharacterized open reading frame YMR152W from S. cerevisiae encodes a novel aldehyde reductase with catalytic functions for reduction of at least six aldehydes...Ymr152wp was classified into the quinone oxidoreductase (QOR) subfamily of the medium-chain dehydrogenase/reductase (MDR) family based on the results of amino acid sequence analysis and phylogenetic analysis. Although Ymr152wp was grouped into the QOR family, no quinone reductase activity was observed using typical quinones.

So it seems members of this family may have evolved different MFs.

The human ortholog of the yeast gene, RTN4IP1, is annotated with:
NADH dehydrogenase (quinone) (non-electrogenic) activity(GO:0050136)	
NADPH dehydrogenase (quinone) activity (GO:0008753)


So I think this family/annotations need splitting?
title: PAINT issue: PTN000746498 - ALCOHOL DEHYDROGENASE RELATED (PTHR11695)

author: marcfeuermann
body: This is not an obvious case. The topology of the tree (1-1-1-1...) does not indicate any ancient duplication events, so it is difficult to determine if, where, and when a loss/gain of function would have occurred. I have revised the annotation by restricting it and associated a general term with the root.
